title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（川島朋也研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Kawashima Tomoya)
educationalGoal: The goal is to elucidate cognitive mechanisms related to attention and memory and provide basic data for developing practical systems. Students will engage in research projects involving psychological experiments and biological signal analysis to explore human mental processes. This includes deepening psychological knowledge and acquiring experimental planning, data analysis, and reproducibility skills. The research applies cognitive psychology to real-world issues, such as driving and polygraph testing.
advice:
Weekly seminars will be held to report and discuss research progress. Active participation in discussions of other lab members' presentations is also expected, fostering a collaborative approach to deepening insights.

Lab members will be required to thoroughly read papers related to their research topics, acquire specialized knowledge, and clarify the positioning of their own research. Understanding the methodologies of previous studies and developing the ability to apply them to one's own research is essential. In addition, detailed experimental and analytical plans should be formulated and accurately expressed in writing. Based on these plans, experiments should be designed and set up with preliminary reviews among lab members.

Data from key experiments will be subjected to hypothesis-driven and exploratory analyses. The results are discussed and, if necessary, new hypotheses are proposed, leading to further experiments. It is important to approach this whole process systematically and steadily.
requiredKnowledge: It is essential to have expertise in the research topic, programming skills to create experiments and analyze data, and an understanding of psychological statistics. In addition to constantly reading academic papers and textbooks to deepen your knowledge, I want you to make an effort to acquire skills by actually getting your hands dirty. I want you to take a proactive approach to learning and to enjoy making new discoveries through your studies.

Understanding the methodologies of previous studies and developing the ability to apply them to one's own research is essential. In addition, detailed experimental and analytical plans should be formulated and accurately expressed in writing. Based on these plans, experiments should be designed and set up with preliminary reviews among lab members.
